components.name: Go crypto/tls sessions on default settings (Go 1.26.0)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Multiple TLS connections in the application use default Go crypto/tls configurations. This means they rely on classical ECDHE key exchange which is vulnerable to Shor's algorithm and needs to be migrated to hybrid post-quantum configurations.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA signatures are used in chatbot/python/chatbot.py and tn-cli/tn-cli.py through GRPC_SSL_CIPHER_SUITES configuration. This is a quantum-vulnerable signature algorithm that needs migration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is used in HMAC operations in server/auth/token/auth_token.go for token authentication. While SHA-256 is cryptographically sound, it's not quantum-safe and should be considered for migration to quantum-safe alternatives.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-256 is used in server/auth/token/auth_token.go for token authentication. While this provides good security today, it's vulnerable to quantum attacks and should be considered for migration.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X.509 certificate parsing is used in server/db/mongodb/adapter.go and server/utils.go for TLS certificate handling. This is a standard practice for TLS configuration but doesn't introduce specific quantum vulnerabilities.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWT signing is used via github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 in go.mod. This indicates the application uses JWT tokens for authentication and authorization, but doesn't directly show implementation details that would indicate quantum vulnerabilities.

properties.name: pqs:context
